healthcareSystem: Universal (Protection Maladie Universelle / PUMA, formerly Sécurité Sociale)
qualityNotes: World-class healthcare system with excellent hospitals and specialists. English is commonly spoken in medical settings in Paris and major cities, less so in rural areas. Reimbursement through French social security requires EU citizenship or a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC) for EU residents.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 9am-8pm weekdays, reduced hours on weekends. Some pharmacies in large cities are open 24/7. Look for the green cross sign.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies (pharmacie) are widely available. Many medications require a prescription. Some OTC items like basic painkillers, antiseptics, and eye drops are available without prescription. Pharmacists are knowledgeable and can advise on minor ailments.
prescriptionRules: EU/Schengen prescriptions are accepted in France. Non-EU prescriptions require a French doctor's consultation. Many common medications in the US require prescriptions here.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine products require a prescription in France. Some codeine products are available behind the pharmacy counter.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances. A Schengen prescription or French doctor's prescription is required. Some ADHD medications are not available in France.

restrictedMeds.name: Sleeping pills (benzodiazepines)
restrictedMeds.note: Benzodiazepines require a prescription. France has strict guidelines around their use.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Medical cannabis was legalized in France in 2021 but remains very restricted and only available through specific channels for a limited number of conditions.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter and prescription (ideally in French or English) for all prescription medications. Bring sufficient supply for your trip. For controlled substances, carry the prescription on you at all times. EU Health Insurance Card (EHIC) for EU citizens.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: While not legally required for short stays, strongly recommended. EU citizens should carry the EHIC/GHIC card for state healthcare access.
travelInsurance.tips: For EU citizens, the EHIC provides access to state healthcare at reduced cost. For non-EU citizens, travel insurance with comprehensive medical coverage is essential. French hospitals may bill directly or require payment upfront.

recommended: Hepatitis A (for close contact with locals or extended stays)
Tick-borne encephalitis (for rural/forest areas in eastern France)
vaccinations.notes: No mandatory vaccinations for travelers. Ensure routine vaccinations (MMR, DTaP, etc.) are up to date.

waterNotes: Tap water is safe to drink throughout France. Bottled water (eau minérale) is widely available if preferred.
foodSafetyTips: France has excellent food safety standards. Cheese, raw milk products, and undercooked meats are popular — these are generally safe but may cause stomach upset if you're not used to them.oysters and shellfish are popular but should be from reputable sources. Wild mushroom foraging is dangerous — only eat mushrooms from trusted sources.
medicalTourismNote: France is a destination for cosmetic surgery and luxury medical retreats. High-quality care at moderate costs compared to the US.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to France. Emergency numbers (15, 17, 18, 112), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccination requirements, and travel insurance advice.

hospitals.notes: Premier international hospital. Fully English-speaking. Direct billing with many insurers.

hospitals.notes: Historic hospital next to Notre-Dame. Emergency department.

hospitals.notes: Largest hospital in Marseille. Major emergency department.

dentalCare.availability: Excellent dental care. French dentists are well-trained and clinics are widespread.
dentalCare.costRange: €23-50 for a consultation; €50-200 for fillings; €80-300 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: French dental care is partially covered by Sécurité Sociale for residents. Tourists pay out-of-pocket. Quality is high throughout the country.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Call 15 (SAMU) for dental emergencies. Hôpitaux universitaires have dental emergency departments (urgences dentaires). Pharmacies can provide pain relief.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: English-speaking therapists available in Paris and major tourist cities. Check Doctolib.fr (France's main healthcare booking platform) for English-speaking practitioners.
mentalHealth.notes: France has CMP (Centre Médico-Psychologique) for free or low-cost mental health consultations. Wait times can be long. Private therapists charge €50-120 per session.

accessibilityInfo.overview: France has been improving accessibility under EU directives. Major tourist attractions and modern buildings are accessible. Older buildings and cobblestone streets can be challenging.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: French hospitals are wheelchair accessible. Most have accessible parking and adapted restrooms.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Paris Métro has limited wheelchair access (line 14 is fully accessible). All buses are accessible. TGV trains have wheelchair spaces. RATP provides accessibility info.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Request a 'fauteuil roulant' (wheelchair) when booking trains. Many museums offer priority access for disabled visitors. The Paris tourist office has accessibility guides.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mask mandates in public spaces. May be required in some healthcare settings.
covidStatus.testing: Antigen tests available at pharmacies (€5-15). PCR available at laboratories (€30-50).
covidStatus.notes: France removed all COVID restrictions. Healthcare professionals may request masks during flu season.

insuranceClaimProcess: French healthcare uses a fee-for-service model. Doctors provide a feuille de soins (care sheet). Keep all receipts and the feuille de soins for insurance claims. EU citizens with EHIC can get partial reimbursement through CPAM. Pharmacies provide itemized receipts (ticket de caisse).
